p039: My systems work includes memory management, interrupts, processes, scheduling, synchronization, and file-system interfaces. I use assembly and debugging tools to inspect calling conventions, stack frames, memory layout, and executable behavior.
p040: In digital hardware, I work with combinational and sequential logic, processor pipelines, forwarding, stalls, exceptions, and memory-mapped I/O.
p041: For parallel programs, I examine thread synchronization, vectorization, cache behavior, GPU memory access, and the overheads that limit speedup.
p043: I work with lexical analysis, parsing, abstract syntax trees, symbol tables, type checking, intermediate representations, control-flow analysis, and register allocation.
p044: My compiler toolkit includes **Flex / JFlex and YACC / BYACC/J**.
p045: In C++, I use ownership, RAII, move semantics, templates, and the STL. I organize software around clear interfaces, manageable dependencies, reproducible builds, and tests that exercise meaningful behavior.

p049: This includes Android lifecycle behavior, Qt signals and slots, database access, and responsive interfaces. With sockets, I account for message framing, partial reads, timeouts, and concurrent connections.
p050: My networking background covers TCP/IP, routing, congestion, DNS, HTTP, authentication, cryptographic primitives, and transport security.
p052: I work with trees, heaps, hashing, string algorithms, graphs, dynamic programming, network flow, and heuristic search. I analyze complexity and choose data structures around the workload.
p053: For machine learning, I can implement classical models and neural networks, derive and check gradients, and evaluate results using appropriate data splits and metrics. My background includes probabilistic models, classification, clustering, CNNs, recurrent networks, and attention.
p054: For search, I work with tokenization, inverted indexes, TF–IDF, BM25, and PageRank. I pay attention to data leakage, error analysis, and reproducibility.
